page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.mn4.large is a general-purpose virtual machine instance belonging to the ecs.mn4 family. It features 2 vCPUs derived from 1 physical Intel Xeon 8269CY core with hyper-threading enabled, running at a clock speed of 2.5 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The instance is configured with 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It operates on a KVM hypervisor with shared CPU allocation, and does not include any local NVMe storage or dedicated GPU hardware.

Performance benchmarks place this instance in the lower tiers of compute and memory capabilities. Single-core stress-ng tests score at 1090.78, while multi-core performance reaches 2067.18, reflecting its shared CPU allocation. Memory bandwidth is limited, with large-block read speeds at 16.93 GB/sec and write speeds at 13.99 GB/sec. Cryptographic and vector operations are supported via hardware flags such as AVX-512 and AES, though overall Passmark and Geekbench scores remain in the bottom 10% to 25% of tested hardware.

Given its shared resource model and lack of local storage, the ecs.mn4.large offers a budget-friendly profile suited for low-intensity workloads. It is appropriate for basic web serving, lightweight background tasks, development environments, and small-scale database operations that do not require sustained high-throughput compute or memory bandwidth.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.mn4.large is a budget-friendly, general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at 2.5 GHz. The instance features a shared CPU allocation model, lacks local storage, and does not include GPU acceleration. Benchmark results indicate modest performance, with Geekbench single-core and multi-core scores of 939.0 and 1598.0 respectively, placing it in the lower performance tiers. It supports AVX-512 and AES instruction sets for basic cryptographic and vector processing. This instance is best suited for low-demand workloads such as lightweight web serving, development environments, and basic background tasks where cost efficiency is prioritized over high-performance compute or high-speed memory bandwidth.
